claim: The premise 'we need time for verification' is probably false for the owner's own accounts: a personal Google app under 100 users needs no verification, and a Meta app in development mode can use the Graph API on accounts holding an app role without App Review (unverified here, but nobody checked). If so, the browser is deferring a non-blocker, and option B (scopes) plus an IG Graph API dev-mode path dominates A; the council should demand that check before any container is built.

Stacking IG browser automation on top of WAHA concentrates ban risk on one corporate owner (Meta) and one person: a flagged owner IG account from a datacenter IP, run alongside an unofficial WhatsApp client, can cascade, and Instagram ToU makes a disabled account ineligible to return. The accepted WAHA risk does not cover this; accepting one ban risk is not accepting a correlated second one on the owner's primary identity.

The interim will not be interim: recipes, a runner service, Protocol adapters, evals, kill switch and audit rows are a large build, and once working, the pressure to replace it with the official API disappears while selector drift creates a permanent maintenance treadmill. 'Deadline to replace each op' has no named owner or trigger, which is the deferral-without-destination the house rules forbid.

Capacity is the weakest number: 3.5 GB available on a prod VPS with 18 containers, Chromium at an unmeasured 0.4-1 GB per context, with a proposed 1.5 GB cap. An OOM on the shared prod box kills arbitrary neighbours, not the browser; there is no dev fleet to rehearse on (prod-only), so first contact is production. Measure it, or run on the laptop, before approving.

The inherited premise is that the official APIs need verification and therefore time, so a browser is the bridge. For the owner's OWN accounts that is likely false: Google personal apps under 100 users need no verification (brief says so), and Meta apps in development mode can use Graph API on accounts holding a role in the app without App Review (unverified here, check before deciding). If both hold, the browser container solves a problem that does not exist for a single-owner first version.

The login and session assumption is fragile: logging in once via noVNC from a datacenter IP with a different fingerprint than the owner's usual device is exactly what triggers Instagram checkpoints and Google re-auth (and DBSC device-bound cookies, Linux coverage unverified). The plan forbids proxies and evasion (legal) while the architect offers per-account proxies, so the design either gets locked out repeatedly or violates the legal red line; the reports disagree and no one reconciled it.

The real goal is validating the PROCESS (what the assistant does with Drive and Instagram), not the transport. Validation needs the capability to exist, and that is cheapest where it already works: Google API scopes in the existing OAuth client, and the laptop Claude-in-Chrome for Instagram (option C). A server container adds a 24/7 availability requirement that nothing in the validation goal demands yet.

Option C is under-weighted: browser automation on the laptop already works and validates the process, which is the owner's stated goal. A server adds only unattended operation, which is precisely the part all four specialists flag as the dangerous one (injection via WhatsApp self-chat, no human watching, bearer-credential sessions on a shared VPS). The strongest case is to validate recipes on the laptop with a human present, and move to a server only when the API path is blocked.

Option A buys the least with the most risk: it stakes the owner's primary Google and Instagram accounts (bearer-session on a datacenter IP, ToS breach, ban/lockout with Instagram being unrecoverable) on a 3.5 GB-free box, to avoid a one-time re-consent screen. The asymmetry is inverted: the saved cost (re-consent) is minutes, the downside is losing the account the assistant runs on. Any browser path should use an expendable Instagram account first.

The floated 'API that receives requests and executes them on Drive through the browser' is the official Drive API reimplemented badly through a UI. Any Drive operation the browser can do, files.create or Sheets/Docs batchUpdate can do deterministically with scoped tokens and an audit trail. Strip this requirement; it is habit from 'as if it were me logged in', not a need.

Sub-decisions 1, 2 and 5 (container per account, noVNC vs SSH, multi-account/client accounts) are premature: the evidence supports exactly one account and one task at a time. Client accounts are a legal red line anyway, so designing multi-tenancy now is inherited generality. Decide only: one owner IG account, SSH port-forward login, recipes only, deadline tied to the Meta verification.

The capacity premise is unmeasured: 'Chromium 0.4-1 GB per context' is an estimate against 3.5 GB available on a box with 18 containers including WAHA, which the Assistant itself depends on. Nobody has specified a first Monday step to measure real RSS of headful Chromium plus Xvfb on this VPS, nor a hard mem_limit/oom_score_adj so a runaway Chrome OOM-kills WAHA rather than itself. Build order must start with a measured spike under a cgroup cap, not the service.

Google write via browser (option A) is the wrong first build: option B is a bounded, testable slice (add scopes to the existing OAuth client, files.create / spreadsheets.values.update / documents.batchUpdate behind the existing Protocol+Fake+Real+factory, one re-consent). The one gating unknown, whether a published-unverified app's refresh token survives 7 days, is cheap to test now and should be Monday task #1, since it decides whether B is viable at all.

The login/2FA channel is undecided between the reports (noVNC behind Cloudflare Access vs SSH port-forward only) and the brief leaves it open, but it blocks everything downstream. An executor needs one answer: SSH port-forward to a private-network VNC bound to loopback, enabled only by a manual command and torn down after, because it adds zero new exposed surface and no Access policy to build or test. Also unspecified: what happens when Instagram throws a checkpoint/challenge from a datacenter IP at first login, which is the likely day-one failure.

Recipes are untestable in CI: the Real browser adapter can only be validated against live Instagram, so there is no red-first test and selector drift is detected only by the proposed daily health recipe, which itself burns account-risk budget. Spec needs a recorded-DOM/fixture layer for recipe logic, a Fake that the Assistant is built against, and a defined acceptance run (which account, how many actions, who watches) before any consumer wires in.

Rollback is not one line: stopping the container leaves a persistent profile volume holding live Instagram/Google session cookies, which is a bearer credential that survives the 'rollback'. The plan needs a kill-switch runbook that is genuinely one command (compose profile off by default, a script that stops the service AND wipes the volume AND revokes the session from the vendor side) and a statement of which of those the owner does by hand.

Option C (laptop runner with the same POST /tasks API and Playwright recipes) is under-weighted as a build step: it lets recipes, Protocols and the Fake be built and exercised this week with zero prod exposure, no capacity risk and no new credential on the VPS. Its real limit is that the WhatsApp-triggered Assistant cannot call it when the laptop is asleep, so it is a staging path to the VPS runner, not a substitute, and should be ordered first.

The premise that Instagram needs a browser until App Review is wrong for the owner's own account: the seed already ships Instagram API with Instagram Login (seed/lib/backend/noctusai_lib/integrations/meta/instagram_login_adapter.py: profile, user/media insights, media, stories, DM read), and a Meta app in development mode serves app-role users without App Review (confirm Standard Access in Meta docs before relying on it). Public third-party profiles are already covered by the seed Apify adapter (integrations/apify). All four reports, the architect's included, missed this, so the browser's real residual gap (likely only actions the Graph API lacks) must be enumerated before any container is built.

The architect's RealBrowserRunner as a seed Real adapter behind InstagramReader/Publisher with a config factory is the wrong level: a seed default reaches every wired product, so a ToS-breaching, single-identity, owner-only path becomes one config flag away from client use, which legal names a red line. Keep any browser path as a platform-tier tool or service (noctus.browser.*) outside the seed factory, and keep the seed Real adapters API-only.

Google write likely needs no browser and maybe no new sensitive scope: drive.file is already in GOOGLE_KITCHEN_SINK_SCOPES (google_scopes.py:81), and the Sheets and Docs APIs accept drive.file for app-created or picker-opened files. Only editing pre-existing owner Sheets/Docs needs the sensitive spreadsheets/documents scopes, so option B should start with drive.file and add sensitive scopes only per measured need; the 7-day token expiry applies to Testing status, not to a published app (verify).

On the login channel I side with security over the architect: SSH port-forward only, no noVNC hostname on the tunnel, because a Cloudflare Access entry in deploy/tunnel/ingress.yml is a persistent public surface fronting a whole-account session for an action needed only on rare re-logins. On container count, both sides are reconcilable: one container, a separate persistent profile per account, launched as a separate browser process per task and never concurrently, meets security's no-shared-profile red line within the measured 3.5 GB.

Trigger and confirmation share one channel: WAHA (unofficial) self-chat both starts a task and carries the owner-typed confirmation, so a compromised or hijacked WAHA session can both request and approve an irreversible IG post/DM or Drive write. Writes need a second factor outside WAHA (for example a platform-admin UI or a code delivered on another channel) or must stay laptop-only until then.

The decision is gated on an unmeasured number (Chromium 0.4-1 GB) on a box with 3.5 GB free shared by 18 containers, and no report gives the interim a sunset. I recommend option C now (laptop Claude in Chrome plus the existing seed IG-Login and Drive API adapters), with a server runner only after a measured RSS trial; any recipe that ships must carry a NOC-REMEDIATE marker naming its official-API replacement and a revisit date as its fitness function.

Reject A for Google: Drive/Sheets/Docs write is an L0 seed capability, not a browser job — extend the existing seed google_drive module (protocol.py/real.py/factory) with a DriveWriter/SheetsWriter/DocsWriter Protocol+Fake+Real via google_scopes_router, consumer #1 the Assistant. It immediately retires two browser consumers (noc-refs-sheet's 'Sheet writer' Chrome role and laptop Drive edits), so B is not a deferral but the cheaper, already-half-built path.

Instagram 'checks' are mostly status 'exists', not 'new': the seed already ships apify InstagramScraper (public profile + posts, Protocol+Fake+Real+factory) and meta/instagram_insights (own-account insights via Instagram Login). Before any IG browser container, the function-to-organ allocation must show which IG jobs neither covers — likely only logged-in actions (DMs, story posting) — and size the browser to that residue only.

Placement: I side with the architect that the runner is a platform service (WAHA class), but the consumer-facing seam must be capability-level seed Protocols (InstagramReader/Publisher, DriveWriter) with the browser as just one Real adapter selected by the factory, never a 'browser task' API that products call. A generic POST /tasks{recipe} exposed to the Assistant would make every product couple to recipe names and break the swap to official APIs ('link, never merge').

Recipes need one home: noc-ig-analysis, noc-refs-sheet and quintoandar-agent/playbook/browser.md are already de facto laptop recipes, and a server runner would create a second copy of each (N=2 -> drift). Define the recipe once (typed, versioned, in the seed/runner package) and have both the laptop Claude-in-Chrome path and the server runner execute that same definition, so option C (laptop first) and the server runner are one capability at two hosts, not two.

Phase it C-then-narrow-A: v1 = option B for Google plus IG via existing apify/insights adapters, with any residual logged-in IG action run by the same runner API on the owner's laptop; promote to a single prod browser container only when a recipe has proven recurring demand. Prod is first-contact (dev fleet dormant) on a box with ~3.5 GB free, so spending ~1.5 GB of prod on an unvalidated demand is the wrong order.

Multi-account variety must be a setting, not a fork: the account is an org-scoped credential/profile key resolved through the existing CredentialStore, one container with a profile per identity (sequential), owner accounts only in v1. Client accounts are a different product tier (NoctusAI as operator, DPA, lawyer gate per legal) and must not be designed into v1 nor sold; leave the seam open, keep the tier closed.

The confirmation-tier flow agents-security proposes (code-built WhatsApp yes/no with exact target + one-time code) is not Assistant-internal: Julia and every later tool-using agent need the same owner-confirm-before-irreversible-action capability. Allocate it to the seed agents/whatsapp layer as a named seam with the Assistant as consumer #1, otherwise it becomes the first 'per-product confirmation' copy.

decision: Option A defeated; B as written incomplete. Recommend B+C API-first, no server browser now: Google API-only (extend seed google_drive with Drive/Sheets/Docs writers, start on drive.file); Instagram via existing seed Instagram Login adapter (Meta dev mode) + Apify; residual logged-in actions on the laptop with the owner present. Server browser-runner only after gates: residual-job demand list, measured RSS under cgroup cap, kill switch + test layer. If built: one container, profile+process per identity, sequential; SSH-only login; recipes-only; expendable accounts; owner accounts only; no proxies/evasion; platform-tier noctus.browser.* outside the seed factory.
biggest_risk: Two unchecked premises (published-unverified Google refresh-token lifetime > 7 days; Meta dev-mode Instagram Login serving the owner without App Review). If either fails quietly, pressure returns to Option A on an unmeasured shared VPS (OOM can kill WAHA) and the owner's primary Instagram can be banned irreversibly.
first_step: Verify both premises before building: a drive.file write through the existing owner OAuth client (start the 7-day clock), and get_profile + list_instagram_conversations via the seed Instagram Login adapter against the owner's account with an app role in dev mode.
